ledger.claim: The platform's recorded distances put this trip at 18.3 km actually driven against a recommended 15.7 km, a deviation of 2.60 km, and the record itself flags the vehicle as leaving the recommended PIE route at the Pasir Ris Drive 3 / TPE slip road and rejoining it only at Braddell Road / Toa Payoh Lorong 6. Under POL-RD-22 the recorded distances govern the measure, and 2.60 km is more than double the 1.0 km tolerance, so the deviation is established and outside tolerance.

The GPS trace independently shows which route was taken: the fixes run along the Tampines Expressway from 14:18:41 and then along Braddell Road from 14:29:41 until the rejoin at Toa Payoh Lorong 6 at 14:40:41, exactly matching the recorded deviation and rejoin events. The route actually driven is the TPE/Braddell loop, not the recommended PIE route the app displayed to the rider.

The driver's explanation that 'PIE got roadworks, LTA announced lane closure, so I avoid' is not borne out by any traffic data. The only advisory on file is a ROADWORK notice for the PIE towards Tuas after the Tampines Avenue 10 exit, valid from 23:00 on 5 September to 05:00 on 6 September, which does not overlap this trip's window of 14:16 to 14:42 on 5 September. Under POL-RD-23 a reroute is traffic-justified only where the advisory overlaps the trip window, so the reroute was not traffic-justified and the driver's asserted reason fails.

The driver also breached the notification obligation. POL-RD-21 requires the driver to inform the rider of the deviation by in-app chat, or verbally with a call recording as evidence, before or at the point of deviation. The chat log for this trip carries zero messages and the trip record shows no in-app calls at all, so there is no notice on the record; a verbal notice with no recording cannot be established. The rider was left to discover the detour for himself.

On the POL-RD-24 matrix the rider recovers the same sum on either available limb. Because the reroute was not traffic-justified and the deviation exceeds 1 km, row (d) applies and refunds the excess distance fare in full; and even if the reroute were treated as traffic-justified, the rider was not informed, so row (b) does the same. The excess distance fare is the deviation distance times the per-km rate without surge: 2.60 km x 0.72 SGD/km = 1.87 SGD. The rider is therefore owed a PARTIAL_REFUND of 1.87 SGD under POL-RD-24.

This dispute is within the AI's power to decide, so the rider should have a ruling rather than an escalation. The contested amount is 6.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, so the AI ruling is final at any confidence, and POL-RD-25's 2 km escalation limb is not applied because the policy's own ai_ruling_max_deviation_applied flag is false; the 2.60 km deviation therefore does not force the case to a human. The facts the matrix needs - the deviation distance, the route taken, the absence of notice and the absence of traffic justification - are all carried by complete artifacts of weight 1.0, so no question is left open under POL-GEN-26.

To be straight with the tribunal: the rider asks for the full 6.00 SGD, but the record does not support that figure and I do not press for a remedy the policy does not give. POL-RD-24 fixes the remedy for an unjustified deviation over tolerance at the excess distance fare, which is 1.87 SGD, and the rider's case is made out to that extent, with PARTIAL_REFUND as the outcome and the balance of the 6.00 SGD not recoverable on this matrix.

The rider asks for 6.00 SGD, but a route deviation does not return the rider's figure: under POL-RD-24 the sum the policy moves is the excess distance fare and nothing more, and on POL-RD-22's measure - the platform's recorded distances, actual 18.3 km minus optimal 15.7 km - the deviation is 2.60 km, so the excess distance fare is 2.60 km x 0.72 SGD per km = 1.87 SGD. The record therefore supports moving 1.87 SGD, not 6.00 SGD, and the balance of the rider's demand is unsupported.

The cap holds however the traffic-justification question is answered. POL-RD-24 row (b) (traffic-justified but the rider not informed) and row (d) (not traffic-justified) both return only the excess distance fare of 1.87 SGD, and the only zero-refund row, (a), requires that the rider was informed and agreed - which the complete chat log (0 messages) and the empty in-app call list do not show. No row of POL-RD-24 reaches the rider's 6.00 SGD, so the contested amount cannot be awarded as claimed.

The payment record confirms the driver's limited exposure: the metered fare of 21.56 SGD was charged and no refund has yet been issued (refund_issued_sgd 0.00), while the itemised excess distance fare is 1.87 SGD. The rider's round figure of 6.00 SGD appears nowhere in the fare breakdown, and under POL-GEN-03 the rider recovers only the part of the charge a policy clause returns - here, the excess distance fare alone.

ruling.explanation:
This is a route-deviation case under POLICY-ROUTE-DEVIATION, decided on the platform's own records, which are all complete artifacts of full weight (1.0). To the rider: your claim is made out in part, but not to the $6.00 you asked for. The platform's recorded distances (EV-TRIP-05015) show 18.3 km actually driven against a recommended 15.7 km, a deviation of 2.60 km under POL-RD-22 — well outside the 1.0 km tolerance. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-05015) confirms the route taken: the fixes run along the TPE from 14:18:41 and along Braddell Road from 14:29:41, rejoining the recommended route at Toa Payoh Lorong 6 at 14:40:41, exactly as the trip record's deviation and rejoin events say. To the driver: your explanation that the PIE had roadworks is not borne out. The only traffic advisory on file (EV-ADVIS-05015-01) is a ROADWORK notice on the PIE towards Tuas valid 23:00–05:00, which does not overlap this trip's window of 14:16–14:42, so under POL-RD-23 the reroute was not traffic-justified and your asserted reason fails. Nor was the rider informed: the chat log (EV-CHAT-05015) carries 0 messages and the trip record shows no in-app calls, so the notice POL-RD-21 requires is absent. On the POL-RD-24 matrix, that is row (d) — not traffic-justified and a deviation over 1 km — which returns the excess distance fare in full; row (b) would give the same result even if the reroute were justified, because it still requires that the rider was informed. The excess distance fare is the deviation distance times the per-km rate without surge: 2.60 km x 0.72 SGD/km = 1.87 SGD. You charged a fare of 21.56 SGD and no refund has been issued (refund_issued_sgd 0.00), so 1.87 SGD is the part of the charge the policy returns and the balance of your 6.00 SGD demand is not recoverable on this matrix. On who decides: the contested amount is 6.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, so the AI ruling is final at any confidence, and POL-RD-25's confidence bar of 0.80 is met; POL-RD-25's 2 km escalation limb does not apply because the policy's own ai_ruling_max_deviation_applied flag is false. No fact needed by the matrix is missing or impaired, so POL-GEN-26 leaves no open question. The advocates on both sides agreed on the governing sum and I accept their reasoning; the rider's request for 6.00 SGD is answered by the matrix, which caps the remedy at 1.87 SGD.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
